implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 0.7 points toward Buffalo Bills of the quote EdgeDesk captured at FanDuel. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 46 sat 2.5 points below the captured total of 48.5.

closing_line.note: The line moved 0.5 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 0 claims held up, 7 held up in direction only and 2 did not. Parts of the read were right and parts were not.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 7.2 and the game finished 3 the away way — 10.2 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 3-point game
variance_markers.text: A game this close is decided inside the noise of any projection. Whichever way it fell, it is weak evidence about either team.

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.
